subject: Re: 🔵{Brand} & MobUpps
body:
Hi RECIPIENT_NAME,
Circling back on my earlier email about first-order acquisition for {Brand}. With DoorDash now holding 67% of US delivery orders in a 74 billion dollar category, the aggregators keep absorbing share, and winning a real ordering customer in US food apps runs 45 to 85 dollars once you price in churn. That is the band where store-density targeting and incrementality decide your true cost per validated order. We run a holdout so paid first orders read as net-new against your organic baseline. Worth comparing that against your current source mix?
angle: fresh angle: US aggregator share concentration (sourced) + US food-app $45-85 CPA band
register_notes: Stage 2 EN food_and_delivery: references prior in first sentence; fresh angle = US aggregator share concentration (DoorDash 67% of orders, $74bn category) plus verified market CPA band $45-85 per acquired food-app user; only DoorDash named, drawn from the parent's market-context set, no out-of-set or cross-border brand as rival; MobUpps holdout reference carries no figure; market context sourced via parent URLs; 1 question mark; no sign-off; no em-dash; no X-not-Y.
